anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly : Concurrent transactions compete for mutually incompatible locks, producing long blocking chains or deadlocks that stall forward progress.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupted, so read or write operations encounter checksum, linkage, or key-order errors.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume nearly all available CPU cycles, leaving little headroom for other sessions or background tasks.

When these three root causes coincide, the system exhibits a multi-layer crisis: 1) sessions accumulate in lock wait queues and deadlock detectors fire; 2) queries that finally obtain a lock may fail with corruption or page-verification errors, triggering repeated retries and rollbacks; 3) the surge of retries, deadlock detection sweeps, and corruption checks drives sustained CPU saturation. Observable symptoms therefore span long transaction latency, victim-abort errors, corruption messages in logs, spikes in lock-wait and CPU wait events, runaway run-queue length at the OS level, and rapidly shrinking throughput despite high thread activity.

Causal chain: corrupted pages or mis-linked index nodes can force the optimizer or storage engine to abandon efficient index probes and fall back to broader scans or page-level recovery logic, greatly extending the time each transaction holds locks. Prolonged lock tenure intensifies blocking, deadlocks, and exponential retry storms. Every retry, deadlock cycle, or corruption re-read translates into additional CPU work—deadlock detection graph walks, lock hash-table manipulation, checksum recalculations, and error-handling logic—that further consumes CPU. CPU saturation in turn slows lock acquisition and flush pacing, lengthening critical sections and making it even harder for waiting transactions to progress, while the persisting corruption continually re-injects failures. The three anomalies therefore reinforce one another to create a self-amplifying degradation that can cripple an OLTP system until corruption is repaired, contention relieved, or compute resources expanded.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
